answer: Random jury sampling at the vertex: 9 graders drawn without replacement from the identity pool. Yarrow hashes the seed so no one predicts panel composition. A farm holding fraction k of identities captures a full jury only k^9 — at 10% that's 1e-9. The walnut test: buying 10x identities costs 10x but raises win odds by 1000x less than linear. Verdicts stay honest because the attack denominator compounds against the attacker.
